title: 一对一沟通怎么问进度、卡点和需要的支持
topic: 回看 Meta（原 Facebook）2020-12 的经理一对一指南，练习倾听同事、明确障碍、支持和下一步；其中 Workplace 等产品术语按历史资料理解。

fullTextParagraphs: 1:1 Guide for Managers
Dedicating time for regular one-on-one connections with your team is one of the best ways to support them, especially when working remotely.
01. Prepare for the 1:1.
Schedule a standing weekly meeting with each person you support.

This meeting can be 30 minutes or longer, or more or less frequent, depending on what you both need. Times of change, before critical project milestones, or during someone’s onboarding period are good times to consider longer or more frequent 1:1s.
Don’t miss 1:1s and try not to reschedule unless requested by the person you support.
Make sure you’re having 1:1s with everyone and in a format (location, structure) and time that works for them.
Keep a shared agenda document and/or use a 1:1 Workplace Group where you can both add topics.
Link to other documents you may use in your 1:1 including goals, expectations, roadmaps, or career plans.
Empower the people you support.

Ask them to contribute agenda topics. Add any topics you have for them after they’ve added theirs. Some people may not know what is important to cover, so be prepared to ask questions to understand work blockers or areas where a status update is needed.
Review action items.
Review action items from the last 1:1 and make sure you have completed the actions you both committed to.
02. During the 1:1.
Check-in (5–15 min).
How are you? How are you feeling about your work this week? What are you excited about / apprehensive about?

Showing deep care for people helps you build trust and better understand someone’s experience. Ask open-ended questions, and then LISTEN. Be open to changing the agenda of the 1:1 if needed, based on how the person is feeling and what support they need in the moment.
Provide support on near-term work (15–30 min).
What’s been going well/not so well this week? Why?

Focus on areas in the work or relationships where you can help. Help people get to solutions by asking open-ended questions, and ask what specific things you can do to help unblock if needed. Ask about projects that are coming up and what they might need from you as they get started.
Additional Questions:
What roadblocks are you running into? How can I help?
What work has given you the most energy?
What work are you finding most challenging? How can I help?
What are some risks that could prohibit you from keeping the work moving?
Ongoing Feedback (10–30 min).
You may not be able to give and receive feedback every week, but the goal is to be as timely as possible.
Giving Recognition:
You did really great work on [project or meeting or presentation] this week.
I noticed that you [name specific behaviors you observed that you know they have been working on].

1:1s are also a great time to recognize people for improvement in areas they have been working on, or successes in XFN relationships, or other project or career-related milestones. Tie recognition to the impact it had, and reinforce that these are behaviors they should keep doing.
Giving Constructive Feedback:
This week I observed an area of growth for you that I’d like to talk about.
This week I got feedback from one of your peers on an area of growth for you that I’d like to discuss.
It’s critically important for everyone to get the ongoing feedback they need to improve. Be specific, and emphasize support for the person’s growth.

Constructive example: One of your peers noted that you missed a deadline this week that slowed down their own work. I’d like to hear how you experienced this, can you tell me a bit more? Although it’s normal to adjust timelines as many things can be out of our control, I’d like to see you communicate any delays more proactively. That looks like [describe expected behavior]. I’m giving you this feedback because we have high expectations, and I know you can reach them.
Asking for Feedback:
It’s important for me to get honest feedback from you. I want to make sure I am supporting you as well as I can. What are 1–2 ways I could support you better?

Asking for feedback helps you improve, and it sets the tone for an open and honest feedback relationship. Remember to thank them for feedback, and find ways for them to see you put their feedback into action.
Additional Questions:
What is one thing I did this week that I could have improved?
What do you wish I did more/less of?
03. After the 1:1.
Periodically ask how your 1:1s are going.
What, if anything, might need to change about the length, frequency, or agenda for these meetings?

Reflect on the 1:1. Ask yourself: “How much did I listen vs. talk?” “Were my feedback examples specific?” “Did I follow up on the things I promised?” “Did I understand and clarify the different types of support the person needs from me to execute?” “Where is my relationship with this person? What could I do differently to strengthen it (if anything)?”
verifiedFacts: Meta 的员工指南或团队工作流程介绍了 一对一沟通怎么问进度、卡点和需要的支持。
本期练习把来源中的沟通方式迁移到常见的项目协作和客户工作场景。

notes.phrase: where you can both add topics
notes.explain: shared agenda 指双方都可以补充内容的议程。
notes.example: I’ve added the budget risk to our shared agenda.

notes.phrase: What roadblocks are you running into?
notes.meaning: 你目前遇到了什么障碍？
notes.explain: run into a roadblock 是询问工作推进中遇到的困难。
notes.example: What roadblocks are you running into with the client approval?

notes.meaning: 我怎样能帮你把事情推进下去？
notes.explain: move something forward 表示推动事情继续进行。
notes.example: What can I do to help move the project forward?

scenario.title: 周会里问清楚进度卡点
english: A teammate’s vendor review is delayed because Legal has not confirmed the contract language.
Ask what is blocking the work, offer specific help, and agree on who will follow up with Legal.
chinese: 同事的供应商评审延期了，因为法务还没确认合同措辞。
问清工作卡在哪里，提出具体支持，并约定由谁跟进法务。

firstAttempt.prompt: 一对一沟通时，同事说供应商方案还卡在法务审核。请用英语问清具体障碍，提出你能做的支持，并确认下一步由谁联系法务。
firstAttempt.sample: What roadblocks are you running into with the Legal review? How can I help? I can check with Legal this afternoon, and we can review the updated terms tomorrow.
firstAttempt.rationale: 先问清卡点，再说自己能做的事，最后约定下一步。

words.example: Let’s review the open items in our one-on-one.
words.translation: 我们在一对一沟通时回顾未完成事项。

words.example: The missing approval is the main roadblock.
words.translation: 缺少审批是目前的主要障碍。

words.collocation: follow up on an action item
words.example: I’ll follow up on the two action items we agreed on.
words.translation: 我会跟进我们约定的两项行动。

taskPhrases.collocation: add topics to a shared agenda
taskPhrases.prompt: 我把预算风险加到一对一议程里了。
taskPhrases.example: I’ve added the budget risk to our shared agenda.
taskPhrases.translation: 我把预算风险加到共同议程里了。
taskPhrases.explain: shared agenda 指双方都可以补充内容的议程。

taskPhrases.word: what roadblocks are you running into?
taskPhrases.meaning: 你目前遇到了什么障碍？

taskPhrases.example: What roadblocks are you running into with the client approval?
taskPhrases.translation: 客户审批方面你现在遇到什么障碍？
taskPhrases.explain: run into a roadblock 是询问工作推进中遇到的困难。

taskPhrases.word: how can I help you move this forward?
taskPhrases.meaning: 我怎样能帮你把事情推进下去？
taskPhrases.collocation: help someone move a project forward
taskPhrases.prompt: 你需要我做什么，才能让项目继续往前走？

taskPhrases.translation: 我可以做什么来帮助项目继续推进？
taskPhrases.explain: move something forward 表示推动事情继续进行。

structure.original: What roadblocks are you running into?
analysis: 用 What roadblocks... 问清楚卡点。
用 How can I help? 邀请对方说出具体支持。
用 I can... 补上自己能采取的行动。
structure.transfer: What roadblocks are you running into with the client brief? I can review the data section today, and we can send the revised version tomorrow.

rewrite.good: What roadblocks are you running into with the Legal review? I can check the open contract questions this afternoon. Let’s reconnect tomorrow and confirm the next step.
rewrite.translation: 法务审核方面你遇到什么障碍？我今天下午可以核对尚未解决的合同问题。我们明天再碰一下，确认下一步。
rewrite.pattern: What roadblocks are you running into with...? I can... Let’s reconnect... and confirm...

cloze.why: run into a roadblock 表示遇到障碍。

choice.prompt: 同事负责的客户上线被法务审批卡住了，哪种回应能让一对一沟通变成实际行动？
options: What roadblocks are you running into? I can check the open questions with Legal today. Let’s review the next step tomorrow.
Let me know if anything changes.
choice.why: 问清卡点、提出具体支持，并约定回看时间。

output.prompt: 同事的客户报价单还缺财务确认，明天中午要发给客户。请用英语问清卡点，提出你可以帮忙核对数字，并约定今天下午 4 点前一起检查。
output.sample: What roadblocks are you running into with the Finance review? I can help check the figures. Let’s review the quote together by 4 p.m. today so we can send it to the client tomorrow morning.
check: 约定检查时间和交付时间
